title: Best Dashboard Developers (2026): Power BI, Tableau and Looker
description: How to hire a dashboard developer for Power BI, Tableau, Looker Studio or Excel: what to include, how to brief it, price drivers and red flags.
intro: A dashboard developer turns your data into a live report you can check at a glance, in tools like Power BI, Tableau, Looker Studio or Excel. A good dashboard answers the questions you ask every week without manual work. Projects go wrong when the dashboard shows lots of charts but no clear answers, the numbers do not match your systems, or it stops updating after delivery. This guide helps you get a dashboard you will actually use.

faq.a: Use the tool your team already has. Power BI suits Microsoft environments, Looker Studio suits Google data, and Tableau is strong for complex visual analysis.
It can, if it connects to live data sources and a refresh schedule is set. Confirm this, and any license it needs.

faq.q: What data access does the developer need?
faq.a: Usually read access to the data sources or exported files. Avoid sharing admin passwords; create limited accounts where possible.

faq.q: How many charts should a dashboard have?
faq.a: Fewer than you think. A handful of key numbers and trends is easier to read than dozens of charts.

faq.q: Can I change it myself later?
faq.a: Ask for a short handover and documentation of data sources and calculations, so you or another developer can maintain it.
